name: Hooton water intake
question: Does adding daily water reduce culture-confirmed recurrent cystitis in premenopausal women who drink low volumes of fluid?

arms.label: usual fluid intake without added water

design.population: Healthy premenopausal women with at least three clinician-attended cystitis episodes in the preceding year (at least one culture-confirmed), daily fluid intake below 1.5 L, and 24-hour urine volume below 1.2 L; an osmolality threshold of at least 500 mOsm/kg was added by amendment.
design.locator: JAMA full text, Methods: Participants, Randomization, Study Procedures; Table 1

verdictNote: Culture-confirmed cystitis episodes were fewer with additional water at 12 months.
takeaway: Adding 1.5 L of water daily to usual intake, versus continuing usual intake alone, reduced mean culture-confirmed cystitis episodes over 12 months from 3.2 to 1.7 per woman in premenopausal low-volume drinkers with recurrent cystitis.

reports.label: Primary 12-month report
reports.citation: Hooton TM, Vecchio M, Iroz A, et al. "Effect of Increased Daily Water Intake in Premenopausal Women With Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Intern Med.* 2018;178(11):1509-1515. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2018.4204
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA full text, Abstract: Design, Setting, and Participants; Methods: Randomization

results.measure: Mean culture-confirmed episodes per woman over 12 months; difference is control minus water

values.exp: 1.7 mean episodes/woman (95% CI 1.5-1.8; n=70 ITT); 111 total episodes
values.ctl: 3.2 mean episodes/woman (95% CI 3.0-3.4; n=70 ITT); 216 total episodes

results.note: At least one symptom and at least 10³ CFU/mL uropathogens in midstream culture; two-sided significance threshold 0.05; intention-to-treat Poisson analysis.
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes: Primary, p 1512; Figure 1
